To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of chiral lithium-metal bases allows enantioselective metalation of ferrocene derivatives.

(1) N,N-diispropylferrocenylamine is a very suitable substrate for the enantioselective formation of a ferrocenyl anion using chiral bases; (2) the enantioselection is strongly dependent on the metal of the base; (3) a dilithium zinc base is particularly suitable, but only in combination with methyl or ethyl ligands.
(S)-1-Phenylethylamine (S-PEA) and (S)-1-(1-Naphthyl)ethylamine (S-NPEA) were used as chiral amines to form lithium amides with lithium and zinc.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of chiral bases, the lithium-metal chiral bases, for enantioselective metalations of ferrocenes.
the development of chiral bases for the enantioselective metalation of ferrocene derivatives.
the development of enantioselective metalations of ferrocenes using lithium-metal chiral bases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enantioselective metalation of substituted ferrocene derivatives with chiral lithium-metal bases is not an easy task.
the use of the dilithium zinc complex with a methyl group in the ligand is the best option for deprotonative enantioselective metalation of N,N-diisoproprylferrocenearboxamide.

the best results were obtained with dimethyl dilithiobis[(S)-1‐phenylethyl‐amido]zincate, which was used to deprotonate methyl ferrocenylcarboxylate, affording the corresponding iodide in 96 % ee and 90 % yield.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best results are obtained with a combination of lithium and zinc in a 1:1 ratio, using the dimethyl dilithum zincate, with a 2:1 molar ratio with respect to the substrate.

dialkyl lithium zincates are the best bases in the deprotonative enantioselective metalation of N,N-diisobutylferrocenylamine, whereas dialkyl bis(amido)lithiums and dialkyl bis(amide)lithium zincates are the most efficient bases in the deprotative enantioselection of N,N-diethylferrocenecarbamide and methyl ferrocenemethanoate.
the use of alkyl ligands in mixed lithium-metal bases is not always beneficial, and that the choice of metal and ligand is crucial.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the choice of the metal in the mixed lithium-metal base is crucial for the enantioselectivity of the deprotonative lithiation of the N,N-diisobutylferrocenylamide and that the alkyl group in the dialkyl bis(1-phenylethylenamino)lithium is important for the enantiodifferentiation in the deprotonation of methyl ferrocenylcarboxylate.

mixed lithium-metal bases can be used for enantioselective reactions of substituted ferrocene derivatives, and that the combination of zinc with lithium can be a useful metal combination in such reactions.
the metalated ferrocene species can be obtained in very good yields and high enantiopurity by using a mixed lithium-metal base.
